dependency: Task 188 runner output, port 8012 eighteen-row proof and GitHub remote readback must exist before any Task 194 automation or queue contract is created.
geometry_policy: No new coordinates, polygons, building footprints or parcel boundaries are created or inferred. Existing points remain search anchors only and every row stays NOT_BOUND.

features.name: Battersea Power Station
features.official_source_evidence: The official destination site presents the restored Power Station with shopping, dining, workplaces and apartments.
features.classification_finding: Mixed Building is supported for the principal Power Station, but the named wider redevelopment covers multiple buildings and plots. Exact geometry must isolate the principal building rather than the complete 42-acre estate.

features.name: Trinity Leeds
features.official_source_evidence: The official Trinity Leeds site identifies the city-centre shopping and leisure destination through stores, dining and visitor information.
features.classification_finding: Retail Property is strongly supported. The centre contains many retail units, so the tracked object is the shopping-centre complex and not an individual shop unit.

features.name: 100 Liverpool Street
features.official_source_evidence: British Land identifies 100 Liverpool Street within Broadgate as a workplace-led commercial building with office accommodation.
features.classification_finding: Office Building is strongly supported. The individual building footprint must remain distinct from the wider Broadgate campus and Liverpool Street station complex.

features.name: Uppark House and Garden
features.official_source_evidence: The National Trust identifies Uppark as a historic house at South Harting, Petersfield, West Sussex.
features.classification_finding: The standalone historic-house identity is supported, but present visitor use and the inclusion of gardens require a taxonomy and principal-building scope decision before preserving Detached Home as a production residential type.

features.name: The Blade, Reading
features.official_source_evidence: Authoritative building references identify The Blade, also known as Abbey Mill House, as a completed Reading high-rise used for office space. A current owner or leasing source remains preferred.
features.classification_finding: Office Building is supported, but primary-source provenance and the exact building footprint remain pending.

features.name: No.1 Spinningfields
features.official_source_evidence: The official Spinningfields estate identity and authoritative building records identify No.1 Spinningfields as a completed Manchester office tower developed by Allied London.
features.classification_finding: Office Building is supported. The tower footprint must remain separate from the wider mixed-use Spinningfields district.
